subject: Chemistry
topic: Why carboxylic acids boil so high: dimers
title: Why Carboxylic Acids Boil So High: Hydrogen-Bonded Dimers
summary: Four molecules of about the same mass boil from 0 °C to 118 °C. Carboxylic acids win because two hydrogen bonds join them into dimers that survive even in the vapour; the same dimers double acetic acid's measured molar mass in benzene.

notes.title: 16 – Why Carboxylic Acids Boil So High

keyPoints: Similar mass (≈ 60), very different b.p.: butane ≈ 0 °C, propanal 49 °C, propan-1-ol 97 °C, **acetic acid 118 °C**.
The O–H of one acid bonds to the C=O oxygen of another, and back: **two hydrogen bonds** make a cyclic **dimer**.
The association is stronger and more extensive than in alcohols, and the dimers survive **even in the vapour**.
In benzene, acetic acid's measured molar mass is about **120**, double the true 60 (abnormal molar mass).
Acids up to **C4** are miscible with water; solubility falls as the chain grows.

blocks.p: Two acid molecules face each other: each O–H hydrogen bonds to the other molecule's C=O oxygen (**O–H···O=C**, twice), closing an eight-membered ring. Breaking this association needs more energy, so the boiling point is high; most acids remain dimers even in the vapour phase and in aprotic solvents such as benzene.

list: Up to four carbons: miscible with water (hydrogen bonds with water).
Longer chains: the hydrocarbon part grows, solubility falls.
Benzoic acid: nearly insoluble in cold water.

quiz.q: Which has the highest boiling point (all M ≈ 60)?
An acetic acid dimer is held together by:
quiz.explain: O–H···O=C on each side of the ring.

quiz.q: The molar mass of acetic acid measured in benzene is about:
quiz.explain: It is mostly dimerised, so colligative methods see about twice 60.

quiz.q: Carboxylic acids in the vapour phase exist mainly as:
quiz.explain: The hydrogen bonds are not broken completely even in the vapour.

quiz.q: Why does solubility in water fall from butanoic to hexanoic acid?
quiz.explain: Only COOH bonds with water; the growing non-polar chain does not.

simulation.reason: A comparison of evidence (four boiling points) and one structural reason (the dimer), carried by the bar chart, the drawn dimer and the quiz. There is no variable a student could usefully manipulate beyond the table.
